findings.recommendation: Log a structured "worker started" event with its settings, and expose a liveness signal (a heartbeat updated each loop turn, or a health endpoint) plus counters for sent, rejected and released jobs and the queue depth or oldest job age, so a stuck or dead worker is noticed before e-mails pile up.
findings.title: The worker exposes no health check, no metric and no start log

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries — after a maximum number of attempts (or a maximum age), dead-letter the job with a reason such as "relay unavailable after N attempts" — and add jitter to the delay so that every released job does not hit the relay at the same moment when it comes back.
findings.title: Temporary failures are retried forever, never dead-lettered

findings.recommendation: Confirm how the mailer classifies a timeout after DATA; if it maps to `Unavailable`, make the retry idempotent (a stable Message-ID per job, checked or deduplicated by the relay) or treat an ambiguous timeout separately from a refused connection.
findings.title: A send that times out after the relay accepted the message is retried and may duplicate the e-mail

findings.evidence: tracing::warn!(job_id = job.id, attempts = job.attempts, delay_s = delay.as_secs(), "relay unavailable, job released");
findings.recommendation: Carry the cause in `SendError::Unavailable` (connection refused, DNS, timeout, SMTP 4xx code and text) and log it as a field, so an operator can tell a relay outage from a network or credential problem.
findings.title: The "relay unavailable" warning carries no cause

findings.recommendation: Read these values from the environment or configuration with the current values as defaults, so the send timeout or retry pace can be tuned during an incident without a release.
findings.title: Poll, timeout and retry settings are hard-coded
